gaps.sentence: 1998 was the year ___ the factory finally closed.
My colleague Anna, ___ joined us in May, has already been promoted.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to Anna; non-defining clauses never use 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The woman ___ won the prize gave a short speech.
gaps.explanation: The gap is the subject pronoun for a person, so 'who' is needed; 'whose' would show possession.

gaps.sentence: It is one of the most impressive buildings ___ I have ever seen.
gaps.explanation: After superlative expressions, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: He showed me the drawer in ___ the keys were kept.
gaps.explanation: 'In which' is the formal relative pattern for things; 'in where' is ungrammatical.

gaps.sentence: The winner, ___ was only seventeen, broke the championship record.
gaps.hint: person as subject after a comma
gaps.explanation: The clause adds extra information about a person, so 'who' is required and 'that' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: We must decide ___ to do next.
gaps.explanation: 'What to do' is the standard pattern meaning 'the thing that we should do'.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.
